driver: Revenue and profit swing driven mainly by investment gains and balance-sheet effects, not by a new growth engine; operating revenue growth is modest.
evidence_quote: Year-to-date Adjusted EBITDA increased to $323.4 million, up from $14.7 million in the prior year period.
red_flags: investment gains drive results; Q2 revenue only +6% y/y; revenue 34% below earlier peak; share count +15.7%
reason: Inflection is from investment gains and holding-company mix, not a structural catalyst; Q2 net income fell sharply y/y.

driver: Nine-month license revenue jump tied to fixed license contracts recognized upfront at signing, plus lower restructuring; quarterly growth only 11.8%, so timing-driven.
evidence_quote: Revenue for fixed contracts is recognized when the software is made available to the customer, which has typically occurred at the time the contract is signed.
red_flags: revenue timing from upfront fixed licenses; Q3 growth slowed to 11.8%; revenue 20% below earlier peak; high tax provision
reason: Acceleration comes from upfront recognition of fixed license deals, an accounting/timing effect; pack shows no new TAM or S-curve driving the numbers.

driver: Pack gives no explanation for TTM revenue +63%; reported operating metrics show subscriber additions and installed capacity falling year over year.
evidence_quote: Subscriber Additions were 19,793, a 31% decrease compared to the second quarter of 2025.
red_flags: revenue driver not explained; subscriber additions down 31%; cash generation guidance cut; tax credit changes (OBBB)
reason: Revenue driver is not explained in the pack and unit volumes are falling, so the numbers do not support a structural catalyst.

driver: Restructuring, US manufacturing, Nexis launch and Europe/C&I demand lifted revenue and margin from a depressed base; part of margin is a tariff refund.
evidence_quote: Revenue grew 20% year over year, GAAP operating loss narrowed significantly, and we returned to non-GAAP operating profitability for the first time since the second quarter of 2023
red_flags: still GAAP operating loss; $13.3M IEEPA tariff benefit in gross margin; revenue 64% below peak; Q3 guide below Q2; US residential softness
reason: Genuine self-help recovery but early, still loss-making and flattered by one-off tariff benefit; guidance points down next quarter.

driver: Revenue up from expansion of multiple large Telos ID programs, plus opex cut 25% (lower stock comp, cost discipline), moving to small profit.
evidence_quote: Revenue increased 32.7% due to 43.7% growth in Security Solutions, driven primarily by the expansion of multiple large programs in Telos ID.
red_flags: 92% revenue from US government; program-based revenue durability unclear; revenue 20% below prior peak; operating margin still negative TTM
reason: Organic program-driven growth with cost cuts and first profit, but contract-based, government-concentrated and still below prior peak; unproven durability.

driver: ATS segment revenue up 230% mainly from a large Asian customer acquired in 2H25 plus more active advertisers; media segment flat to declining.
evidence_quote: primarily due to a large customer in Asia that we acquired in the second half of 2025, and increases in monthly active advertisers and revenue per monthly active advertiser
red_flags: single large customer drives growth; gross margin down 17pp (cost of revenue up 210%); media segment operating loss; TelevisaUnivision agreements expire 2026-12-31; revenue 40% below earlier peak
reason: Structural-looking ATS expansion with real segment profit, but dependent on one large customer, low gross margin and expiring Univision agreements.

driver: Margin and profit recovery from cost cuts and higher OEM volume (order timing) plus record commercial channel; management says H2 will moderate.
evidence_quote: continued strength in the OEM Channel supported by favorable US Monovisc and Orthovisc sales.
red_flags: OEM order timing; H2 moderation guided; 10-Q MD&A missing from pack; revenue still 29% below peak
reason: Self-help margin gains are real but revenue lift leans on OEM timing and the pack lacks MD&A; early and unproven.

driver: AI-chip final-test services started in Malaysia in FY2026 lifted the SBS segment 99%, now 78% of revenue; gross margin fell sharply.
evidence_quote: The SBS segment reported revenue growth across all subsidiaries except for our China operations, primarily supported by stronger demand for artificial intelligence
red_flags: gross margin down 8.5 pp to 16.6%; operating loss; tiny company, $62.6M revenue; memory component shortage raising costs
reason: Growth is organic and tied to AI test demand, but profitability is worsening and the ramp is unproven at this scale.

driver: Revenue spike from labor disruption (strike) staffing demand in Q1 plus travel nurse rebound; management calls these events unpredictable.
evidence_quote: labor disruption events are unpredictable and have driven spikes in demand and related financial outcomes when they happen
red_flags: labor disruption revenue is non-recurring; revenue 37% below peak; Q2 revenue only +2% YoY
reason: Growth is driven by temporary strike-staffing spikes and a staffing-cycle rebound, not a structural change.

driver: Comparable sales up 12% on current inventory and full-price selling, with fewer stores and e-com growth; gross margin and operating income recovering.
evidence_quote: Total comparable net sales, including both physical stores and e-com, increased by 12.1%.
red_flags: TTM revenue still 24.8% below earlier peak; TTM operating margin only 0.1%; store count shrinking; mall apparel retail, consumer spending risk
reason: Genuine self-help recovery in comps and margins, but the base is small, TTM profit near zero and the gains are unproven over a full cycle.

driver: Revenue surge largely from the Mercury credit card platform acquisition closed September 2025, adding a top-25 card program.
evidence_quote: On September 11, 2025, the Company acquired all outstanding equity interests of Mercury, a leading data- and tech-centric credit card platform
red_flags: growth from acquisition; subprime consumer credit exposure; heavy regulation
reason: Inorganic growth from an acquisition is non-structural per rules, and the pack shows no organic driver.

driver: Demand tied to met coal, oil and iron ore prices at customer projects; data center demand mentioned only as emerging, mainly in the US.
evidence_quote: Prices for the commodities that our customers produce remained elevated through the first nine months of 2026
red_flags: commodity price dependence; revenue 32% below earlier peak; data center demand not quantified
reason: Commodity-linked cycle; revenue still far below peak and the new data center demand is not shown in the numbers.

driver: Higher frac sand volumes and slightly higher prices as oilfield customers increased activity; industrial products segment is small.
evidence_quote: During the first half of 2026, we experienced an increase in the volume of sand sold as customers increased their activity.
red_flags: oilfield cycle exposure; operating margin only 2.0%; free cash flow negative in Q2
reason: Growth is an activity-cycle effect in a commodity-like business; AI/LNG demand is only described as something being watched.

driver: Revenue growth attributed only to higher volume, mainly services; large retailer project work, but pack gives no durable structural driver.
evidence_quote: The resulting increase in total revenue was due to increased revenue in all three segments due to higher volume.
red_flags: project-based, lumpy revenue; dependence on one large retailer; share count +25%; FY Q2 revenue expected to fall
reason: Pack explains growth only as higher volume from project work; no structural catalyst shown and revenue still 39% below peak.

driver: Refining margins very strong plus Martinez refinery back to full operations after fire, supported by insurance proceeds of $1.25B.
evidence_quote: while refining fundamentals remained exceptionally strong
red_flags: commodity refining cycle; fire recovery and insurance proceeds; debt extinguishment losses
reason: Profit jump is refining-margin cycle and recovery from the Martinez fire with insurance offsets; non-structural.

driver: Medicare Advantage membership up 48% via footprint expansion (five states, 203 counties) plus higher premium; margins turning slightly positive.
evidence_quote: driven primarily by growth in our Medicare Advantage membership and higher per-member premium.
red_flags: Star rating win under CMS appeal; benefit expense ratio about 87%; thin operating margin; interim CFO
reason: Fast organic membership growth and profitability turn, but margins are thin and the 4.5 Star benefit depends on a court ruling now being appealed.

driver: Operating profit jump driven largely by roughly $15M IEEPA tariff refunds booked in cost of sales, plus price increases in Fishing.
evidence_quote: Refunds received through July 3, 2026 totaled approximately $15,600, including interest.
red_flags: tariff refund one-off; Camping segment declining; revenue 15% below earlier peak
reason: Margin inflection is substantially a non-recurring tariff refund; underlying quarterly sales growth is only 5%.

driver: App Growth Platform (ad exchange, brand advertising) growing 56% on new publishers/demand partners, now about a third of revenue, lifting margins.
evidence_quote: App Growth Platform revenue increased by $20,304, or 55.9%, for the three months ended June 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025
red_flags: interest rate 11.65% on debt; net loss; warrant derivative loss; share count +13%; revenue 40% below prior peak
reason: Organic fast-growing segment is material and margins improved, but heavy leverage, dilution and net losses; AGP growth partly from large partners.

driver: Headline catalyst is a $719M litigation judgment against Papaya (collection uncertain); underlying revenue growth from RZR ad-tech is modest, losses remain large.
evidence_quote: The court issued an opinion and order awarding $719 million in disgorgement of unjust profits, plus approximately $10.1 million in fees and costs to Skillz on July 27, 2026.
red_flags: litigation award, collection uncertain, appeal/Chapter 15; operating margin -53%; Tether termination dispute; revenue 70% below peak
reason: Value case rests on a litigation judgment, a one-off; operating business still deeply loss-making and facing Tether risk.

driver: Aerospace and military demand recovery with order timing on V-22 and Black Hawk programs; gross profit actually fell on LIFO cost.
evidence_quote: Recovery in the aerospace markets was the primary contributor to the increased bookings.
red_flags: order timing; gross profit down YoY; prior-year ERC benefit distorts comparison; skilled labor shortage
reason: Cyclical aerospace recovery and timing effects, not structural; latest quarter profit is nominal.

driver: Revenue up with fuel prices and volatility; Marine profit up on higher bunker prices; Land exits and restructuring help but volume is down 6%.
evidence_quote: which continue to benefit from increased bunker fuel prices and global supply dynamics.
red_flags: revenue growth is fuel price pass-through; volume down 6%; operating margin about zero; Universal TSS acquisition contributes to aviation
reason: Commodity price and volatility driven; restructuring is real but thin-margin fuel distributor with falling volume.

driver: Claims intelligence solutions (Data iSight, Surprise Bill Services) grew 13.7% while other segments shrank; total growth only 6.6%.
evidence_quote: This increase in revenue was primarily due to an increase in Data iSight and Surprise Bill Services.
red_flags: total revenue growth only 6.6%; interest expense $100M vs operating income $23M; net loss $59M in Q2; legal costs on antitrust matters; other segments declining
reason: Growth is modest and the segment is already most of revenue; interest burden wipes out operating income, so no 10x setup.

driver: Sales up mainly on semiconductor wafer-fab equipment demand and RF/wireless components; wind and storage smaller contributors.
evidence_quote: The increase in PMT was due to strong growth from our customers in the semiconductor wafer fab industry and continued growth in our RF & Wireless components business.
red_flags: semiconductor capex cycle exposure; small scale, 4.4% operating margin; tariff exposure
reason: Growth tracks industry demand recovery in wafer fab and RF; GES (new area) is only about 14% of sales, not a distinct S-curve.

driver: LINZESS net sales up on net price from eliminated inflationary rebates and rebate reserve timing, with only 4% demand growth.
evidence_quote: significantly improved net price due to elimination of inflationary rebates and favorable time-phasing of gross-to-net rebate reserves
red_flags: single-product dependence; price and accounting timing effect; partner AbbVie controls US sales; pipeline asset needs confirmatory Phase 3
reason: Profit lift comes from pricing and reserve timing on a mature product, not a new structural growth driver.

driver: Management credits optical networking and hyperscaler customers, but the pack gives no revenue split and quarterly growth is only 6.1%.
evidence_quote: Demand across our end markets remained strong during the quarter led by the results of our Optical Networking Solutions business.
red_flags: optical share of revenue not quantified; GAAP operating margin negative; revenue 15.7% below earlier peak; German minority appraisal litigation
reason: Optimism without numbers tying growth to a new segment; recent growth modest and GAAP loss-making.

driver: Gross margin jump is mostly an IEEPA tariff refund; underlying margin about 48%. Sales up 11.7%; OVO acquisition closed after quarter end.
evidence_quote: The gross margin rate, excluding the benefit of the tariff refund, was 48.2% in line with the Company's expectations.
red_flags: tariff refund one-off; SG&A +40.7%; OVO acquisition costs and integration; tax expense normalising
reason: Margin improvement is a one-time tariff refund; underlying growth is single/low double digit and the next leg is an acquisition.

driver: Revenue jump is the Rex regional airline acquired Dec 2025 plus new leasing units; legacy segments flat to down and operating loss widened.
evidence_quote: representing a full quarter of Rex operations, which was acquired on December 18, 2025
red_flags: growth from acquisition; consolidated operating loss $12.8M; ground support revenue -76%
reason: Growth is inorganic from the Rex acquisition and profitability deteriorated.

driver: Higher refining crack spreads and fuel prices lifted refining margin and revenue; some help from cost cuts under the optimization plan.
evidence_quote: which reflects an increase in refining margin driven by increased crack spreads
red_flags: commodity crack spread dependence; net loss YTD; heavy debt; revenue 40% below peak
reason: Numbers driven by refining margin cycle and fuel prices; non-structural.

driver: Platform, cloud and managed services adopted by new customers, taking share from legacy vendors, plus per-subscriber software growth; margin and profit improving.
evidence_quote: The increase in appliance revenue was primarily due to the adoption of our platform, cloud and managed services by new customers
red_flags: growth ~28%, not 10x pace; gross margin down 170 bp in Q2 on memory costs; one customer 12% of Q2 revenue; software share of revenue not shown in pack
reason: Organic, share-taking platform growth with rising operating margin, but the pack does not show the new platform's revenue share and growth is moderate.

driver: China ICL sales jumped from $5.3M to $52.3M per quarter on share gains and EVO+ mix; rest of world grew about 6%.
evidence_quote: Net sales to our two distributors in China were $52.3 million for the three months ended July 3, 2026, compared to net sales of $5.3 million in the prior-year period.
red_flags: China over 50% of revenue via two distributors; TTM revenue only back to prior peak (-0.5%); ERP implementation issues; prior-year base depressed; tariff pressure on margin
reason: Numbers match a China-led surge, but concentration, recovery-to-peak base and ERP problems make it unproven as a durable structural story.

driver: Higher construction activity across water, electrical and gas transmission, helped by better spring weather and recovery in transmission work.
evidence_quote: The increase was primarily driven by increased work across all segments, particularly Gas & Petroleum Transmission.
red_flags: low-margin contractor; gross margin fell to 11.0%; backlog fell from $325M to $287M in quarter; share count +6%
reason: Project-activity and timing effect in a thin-margin contractor; data-center/water-replacement commentary is optimism, not shown in numbers.

driver: Higher shipments to two existing major US buyers plus a small new Korean customer; no new product or market that is material.
evidence_quote: The increase was mainly due to an increase in shipments to our two major buyers in the U.S. and the introduction of a new customer in Korea.
red_flags: VF Corporation 57% of sales; thin 16% gross margin; tariff and Middle East logistics risk; Q2 gross margin guided down to 14-15%
reason: Growth is volume from existing concentrated customers; Korea only 4% of sales, so no structural catalyst shown.

driver: Capitated lives and specialty pharmacy growth, Florida delegated arrangements, first delegated contracts in Nevada and Oregon, California exclusivity.
evidence_quote: driven by continued strength in prescription fill volumes as we bring new capitated lives onto the platform, along with the ongoing ramp of our Florida delegated arrangements.
red_flags: still net loss; adjusted EBITDA barely positive; cash only $41.1M; diluted shares up 20%; risk-bearing medical loss ratio
reason: Expansion into new states and delegated contracts is structural and growing 35%, but profitability is marginal and balance sheet thin.

driver: TTM growth reflects 2025 baseplate demand; latest quarter revenue grew only 3% with operating loss and lower gross margin.
evidence_quote: Revenues totaled $8,309 in Q2 2026 compared with $8,078 generated in Q2 2025, an increase of 3%.
red_flags: current growth only 3%; operating loss; gross margin 15% vs 17%; share count +24%; first-half revenue declined
reason: Growth has stalled in 2026 and margins fell; no new structural driver shown in the numbers.

driver: Pack contains only forward-looking boilerplate; no explanation of the numbers.
evidence_quote: Comparisons of results for current and any prior periods are not intended to express any future trends or indications of future performance
red_flags: MD&A text not captured; TTM revenue flat (-0.4%); revenue 33% below peak
reason: Pack gives no driver and revenue is flat; nothing supports a catalyst.

driver: Ethanol crush margins rose to $0.33/gal from $0.11 on export demand and tight inventories; 45Z credits and essential ingredient prices help.
evidence_quote: The second quarter’s market crush margins improved significantly to $0.33 per gallon from $0.11 per gallon in the same period last year.
red_flags: commodity crush margin dependence; revenue growth only 1%; ATM equity program; revenue 44% below peak
reason: Profit swing is commodity margin recovery, not a structural change; TTM revenue nearly flat.

driver: Record US portfolio purchases in a favorable supply market lift collections and revenue; leverage-funded purchasing.
evidence_quote: Favorable purchasing conditions continue in U.S. market
red_flags: debt-funded portfolio purchasing; market-condition dependent; $30.5M refinancing costs
reason: Growth reflects a favorable credit cycle and debt-funded buying, not a new product or market; guided growth is 8-10%.

driver: Pack gives only financial statements; revenue rose sharply but losses widened and the cause is not explained.
evidence_quote: Total operating revenues 1,355 886 3,626 2,727
red_flags: operating loss widening; stockholders equity only $37M; Early Return Agreements charges $180M; fuel and aircraft rent costs surging; airline cyclicality
reason: Revenue driver not explained and losses are growing with thin equity; an airline, cyclical and capital intensive.

driver: Pack does not explain the revenue rise; it describes production cuts, workforce reduction and a cash-flow reset.
evidence_quote: we have reduced our production volume to better align production plans with anticipated demand to improve working capital
red_flags: operating margin -263.6%; revenue driver not explained; production cut and workforce reduction; heavy debt draws ($800M in July); diluted shares +16.2%
reason: Driver is not explained, losses are very large, and management is cutting production to conserve cash.

driver: Revenue and margin lifted by execution on newer, larger, higher-margin projects, plus a $27.5M drop in share-based compensation expense.
evidence_quote: primarily driven by increased project execution activities on certain newer, larger and higher-margin projects that have significant scope of work remaining.
red_flags: backlog down 6% YoY; new awards fell to $2.3B from $5.0B in 1H; part of EPS gain from lower share-based comp; lumpy fixed-price project risk
reason: Margin mix shift is real but project-driven and lumpy; backlog and awards are shrinking and SBC drop flatters GAAP earnings.

driver: Pack's revenue-driver section is only a forward-looking risk list; it gives no reason for the 14% sales rise.
evidence_quote: economic conditions that affect the telecommunications sector, the data communications sector, certain technology sectors
red_flags: driver not explained; small growth, revenue below earlier peak; TTM revenue only $82.8M; operating cash flow weak, inventory up
reason: No stated driver in the pack and growth is modest; nothing supports a structural catalyst.

driver: Net sales surge mostly from higher metal pass-through prices; conversion revenue rose about 25% on demand, pricing and mix.
evidence_quote: Our results reflected continued strength in customer demand, improved Conversion Revenue, and favorable pricing and product mix.
red_flags: revenue inflated by aluminum metal prices; metal price lag swings; net income down year over year in the quarter
reason: Top-line growth is largely commodity pass-through; underlying conversion growth is modest and not a new structural driver.

driver: Brand Portfolio growth is largely the Stuart Weitzman acquisition; gross margin boosted by tariff refunds; Famous Footwear declining.
evidence_quote: Brand Portfolio net sales increased 23.6% to last year, and 8.2% when excluding Stuart Weitzman.
red_flags: growth from acquisition; tariff refund $55.6M one-off; Famous Footwear comps -5.9%; consumer weakness
reason: Inorganic growth plus one-off tariff refunds; core retail business is shrinking.

driver: Semiconductor equipment demand upswing lifted Products revenue; margin gains are modest and company is raising equity via ATM.
evidence_quote: primarily due to an increase in customer demand, driven by an overall market improvement in the semiconductor industry
red_flags: thin margins (op margin 4.3%); ATM equity issuance; semiconductor cycle exposure
reason: Growth is attributed to a semiconductor market improvement, a cyclical upswing.

driver: New CEO and WIN-EXECUTE-DELIVER plan: better project execution lifted gross margin to 7.3%, SG&A cut 11%, revenue grew 14%; still loss-making.
evidence_quote: an increase in gross margin to 7.3% in fiscal 2026 from 5.2% in fiscal 2025
red_flags: backlog down 31% to $953M; book-to-bill 0.7x; operating margin still negative; CEO just changed July 2026
reason: Self-help margin repair is visible, but backlog is shrinking, profits are barely positive and the new CEO is unproven.

driver: Higher shipments, alloy and energy surcharges, and price/mix from aerospace and defense; sales up 12%, but gross profit only up 6%.
evidence_quote: The increase in net sales was driven by higher volume of shipments and related surcharges and improved price/mix.
red_flags: surcharge pass-through; commodity exposure; rising manufacturing costs; revenue 27% below peak
reason: Steel cycle and surcharge-driven growth with modest profit gain; defense mix is a plus but not yet a material new curve.

driver: Steady 7% sales growth with margin gains from execution; no new product, market or cycle trigger described.
evidence_quote: Sales of $234.6 million, 7.1% growth from $219.0 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, despite one less week
red_flags: backlog down year over year; new orders down; tariff cost pressure; mature growth profile
reason: Incremental growth in a mature display business; targets are 7-10% revenue CAGR, nowhere near a 10x profile.

driver: Revenue is roughly flat (+0.4% TTM); profit swing comes from debt extinguishment gain and lower stock comp, not from a growth catalyst.
evidence_quote: we delivered $118.1 million and $225.6 million in revenue, respectively, a 5% and 1% increase
red_flags: Q2 net income driven by $59.3M debt gain; labor market subdued; revenue 50% below peak
reason: No growth catalyst; flat revenue and one-time debt gain inflate earnings.

driver: No inflection explained: Experiential growth offset by Branded Services declines; operating income fell and net loss widened.
evidence_quote: delivered strong second-quarter performance, supported by continued favorable demand and execution.
red_flags: Q2 operating income down 83%; net loss $62.7M; Branded Services revenue down 20%; heavy interest expense; Adjusted EBITDA down 12%
reason: Revenue growth only 2% and profitability deteriorating in Q2; no catalyst supports a structural inflection.

driver: Quarterly revenue doubled on more commercial orders, but pack gives no durable driver; two customers are 84% of revenue.
evidence_quote: The increase was due to increased commercial orders, which more than offset variability in the timing of federal awards during the period.
red_flags: two customers 84% of revenue; TTM revenue 24.5% below peak; operating loss; warrant and earnout liabilities; lumpy transactional revenue
reason: Small lumpy base, extreme customer concentration and revenue still below peak; no evidenced structural catalyst.

driver: Pre-revenue clinical-stage biotech; revenue is from the Lilly collaboration and the pack does not explain its recent growth.
evidence_quote: We do not have any products approved for sale and have not generated any revenue from product sales.
red_flags: no approved products; collaboration revenue only; operating margin -198%; equity raised with warrants, shares +11%; Lilly research term expires Dec 2026
reason: Revenue growth is collaboration accounting, not a commercial inflection; pack gives no operating catalyst tied to the numbers.

driver: Semiconductor assembly equipment upcycle; sequential and YoY revenue rebound as demand improves across end markets.
evidence_quote: We see strong sequential growth in the third quarter and demand conditions continue to improve across all end markets.
red_flags: 56% of revenue from China-headquartered customers; interim CEO; management cites semiconductor cycle
reason: Recovery is a cyclical equipment upswing, which the company itself describes as cyclical.

driver: Census up about 6% and margin recovery shown, but pack does not explain what drove the margin gain beyond general value initiatives.
evidence_quote: Center-level Contribution Margin (1) as a percent of revenue of 23.0%, increased 5.0 percentage points compared to 18.0% in 2025
red_flags: Colorado Medicaid rate cut expected FY27; California PACE moratorium; rising cost of care and labor pressure; net loss for year
reason: Margin improvement is shown but not attributed to a specific structural catalyst in the pack, and FY27 rate pressure is flagged.

driver: Aluminum price increases passed through, aerospace destocking easing, and tight North American auto sheet supply lifting revenue.
evidence_quote: Aerospace demand has improved. The destocking of aluminum products in the supply chain also continues to ease.
red_flags: metal price pass-through inflates revenue; tariff exposure; cyclical end markets
reason: Revenue growth is largely metal pricing and cycle recovery, which is non-structural.

driver: Operating income inflection is a $229.9M gain on the US tower portfolio sale; underlying revenue growth is 2%.
evidence_quote: The increase reflects a $229.9 million gain recorded on the initial closing
red_flags: asset-sale gain drives operating margin; revenue growth 2%; consumer fixed revenue declining
reason: Margin spike is a one-time asset sale gain; revenue is flat and below earlier peak.

driver: TTM growth is stale; revenue collapsed in 2026 after Medicare skin-substitute reimbursement changes, so the inflection is negative.
evidence_quote: Net revenue of $42.8 million for the second quarter of 2026, a decrease of $58.0 million compared to net revenue of $100.8 million for the second quarter of 2025.
red_flags: Q2 revenue -58% y/y; net loss $96M in Q2; reimbursement policy risk; Dermagraft sales suspended
reason: Current revenue is collapsing; the positive TTM figure reflects the pre-collapse period.

driver: Higher new crane sales in Europe/Middle East plus an $11.8M one-time tariff refund lifting gross margin; Americas down.
evidence_quote: This increase was primarily attributable to $69.0 million of higher new machine sales in the Company's EURAF and MEAP segments
red_flags: tariff refund one-off boosts margin; Americas sales -6.6%; operating margin only 3.1%
reason: Machinery cycle recovery plus tariff refund one-off; no structural catalyst.

driver: Lymphedema line grew 12% in Q2 with gross margin 76%; Nimbl replacing Entre is a product refresh, not shown as a fast new S-curve.
evidence_quote: an increase of $7.7 million, or 12%, in sales and rentals of the lymphedema product line
red_flags: Q2 revenue growth only 9%; airway clearance sales down 7%; small acquisition (LymphaTech) in 2026; reimbursement dependence
reason: Steady mid-teens core growth with no new segment materially outgrowing the core; pack shows no step-change catalyst.

driver: Higher sales volume in a semiconductor and passives upcycle, with book-to-bill 1.32; margins up on volume absorption.
evidence_quote: Net revenues increased versus the prior fiscal quarter and the prior year periods primarily due to higher sales volume.
red_flags: industry upcycle dependence; revenue still 6% below earlier peak; equity raise of $830M dilutes; heavy capex
reason: Management itself frames this as an upcycle; cyclical recovery rather than a new structural growth driver.

driver: Newly launched Emrosi grew 189% to 44% of Q2 product revenue, more than explaining total growth while legacy Qbrexza and others declined.
evidence_quote: The increase was driven by continued commercial demand momentum for Emrosi ® , which generated revenues of $8.1 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
red_flags: single-product dependence; legacy products declining (Qbrexza -26%); share count +19%; cash only $25.6M and interest-bearing debt; controlled by Fortress
reason: Numbers match a new product ramp: Emrosi is material, TRx rising, operating income turned positive. Small scale and dilution are risks to monitor.

driver: Electronic component distribution upcycle with higher volumes and higher-priced components, including memory price increases; margins thin.
evidence_quote: mainly attributable to increased sales volumes and the mix of higher-priced components and to a lesser extent from increase in prices for certain memory-related products
red_flags: gross margin declined; operating margin 2.6%; component price cycle exposure
reason: Distributor growth tied to component demand and pricing cycle with thin, flat margins.

driver: New CEO restored software reliability, reorganized operations, exited a contract manufacturer and resumed new products; margins and net income recovered.
evidence_quote: reorganized our operations to improve our efficiency and effectiveness and recommitted to delivering the kind of premium experience our customers expect
red_flags: tariff exposure; memory chip cost pressure from AI buildout; revenue 17% below peak; TTM revenue growth only 5.6%
reason: Genuine self-help turnaround with margin recovery, but revenue growth is small and tariff and component-cost risks remain.

driver: LEO satellite airtime (Starlink and OneWeb resale) growing fast while legacy VSAT shrinks; LEO now over half of airtime revenue.
evidence_quote: LEO service sales represented over 55% of airtime service sales, as compared to less than 32% for the three months ended June 30, 2025.
red_flags: still operating loss; dependence on Starlink as supplier and competitor; low service gross margin; VSAT decline; revenue 28% below peak
reason: Genuine mix shift to LEO driving 27% growth, but resale economics are thin, operating income is negative and platform control sits with Starlink.

driver: Sales growth reflects fuel prices (volume flat at 2.0B gallons); profit up on higher fuel margins and favorable market conditions.
evidence_quote: Product margin from gasoline distribution increased to $175.0 million from $137.9 million in the year-earlier period, primarily due to higher fuel margins (cents per gallon).
red_flags: volume flat, revenue is price; commodity margin dependence; operating margin 1.5%
reason: Commodity price and margin cycle in a low-margin fuel distributor; no structural change.

driver: Tungsten raw-material price spike plus pricing actions and volume recovery drove gross profit; favorable timing of pricing versus costs.
evidence_quote: The increase in gross profit was driven by the favorable timing of raw material-related pricing compared to costs of approximately $316 million
red_flags: margin driven by commodity price timing; operating cash flow negative; working capital build; tariffs and inflation
reason: Profit surge is a raw-material pricing and cycle effect, not a structural change; cash flow went negative.

driver: Revenue is declining; reported profit jump is from a $132M gain on sale of data centers and lower depreciation.
evidence_quote: Cogent sold ten of its owned data centers for net proceeds of $224.2 million resulting in a gain of $130.7 million in Q2 2026.
red_flags: service revenue -4.3%; net leverage 6.23x; enterprise customers and connections shrinking
reason: Earnings inflection is from asset-sale gains while revenue shrinks.

driver: Revenue jump comes from the November 2025 merger with Mesa Air Group, adding Mesa's fleet and flying to results.
evidence_quote: beginning on November 25, 2025, also includes the operations, financial position, and cash flows of the former entity Mesa Air Group, Inc.
red_flags: growth from merger; diluted shares up 15%; three partner airlines are all revenue; new union representation of maintenance staff
reason: Revenue growth of about 61% is inorganic from the Mesa merger; non-structural per criteria.

driver: Pricing and volume gains in Print and Advanced Materials and Chemicals (up 40%), lower interest and impairments lifting profit.
